```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(readr)

options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')
```

```{r message=FALSE}
# Import data
decision_tasks_raw <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "Data_decision_task_online.csv"))
estimates_raw <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "Matlab_Results_OHI_online.csv"))
estimates_decision_level_raw <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "Matlab_Results_OHI_online_decision_level.csv"))
quality_controls <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "Quality_Controls.csv"))
garp_results <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "GARP_results_online_sample.csv"))
survey_data <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "Data_online_survey.csv"))

complete_sl <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "1_raw", "2023_11_Bilendi", "Completes_sl12.csv"),
                        col_types = list(participant_label = col_character()))
complete_fl <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "1_raw", "2023_11_Bilendi", "Completes_fl.csv"),
                        col_types = list(participant_label = col_character()))
complete_fl2 <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "1_raw", "2024_12_Dynata", "Completes_fl2.csv"),
                        col_types = list(participant_label = col_character()))

completes <- rbind(complete_sl, complete_fl, complete_fl2)

# Add participant code to 'completes'
completes <- completes %>% left_join(y = survey_data[, c("participant_code", "participant_label")], by = c("participant_label"))

# Define a table with the country abbreviations
country_abrv <- tribble(
  ~country_abrv,  ~session_label, ~region_name,
  "ID", "Indonesia", "Indonesia",
  "ID", "indonesia", "Indonesia",
  "CA", "canada-en", "Canada",
  "CA", "canada-fr", "Canada",
  "CA", "canada", "Canada",
  "AU", "australia", "Australia",
  "CN", "china", "China",
  "FR", "france", "France",
  "DE", "germany", "Germany",
  "IN", "india", "India",
  "JA", "japan", "Japan",
  "NI", "nigeria", "Nigeria",
  "PE", "peru", "Peru",
  "PH", "philippines", "Philippines",
  "US", "usa" , "United States",
)

# List of data names
data_names <- c("estimates_decision_level_raw",
                "estimates_raw")

# Apply na.omit to all imported data
for (name in data_names) {
  assign(name, na.omit(get(name)))
}

#### Quality exclusions before commencing with the analysis
quality_controls <- quality_controls %>%
  left_join(
    y = garp_results,
    by = c("participant_code")) %>%
  left_join(
    y = estimates_raw[, c("participant_code", "task_number", "unipref")],
    by = c("participant_code", "task_number"))

eligible_tasks <- quality_controls %>%
  filter(participant_code %in% completes$participant_code) %>%
  group_by(participant_code) %>% filter(n() < 5) %>% ungroup() %>% # Filter for participants with 5 tasks (only the 60 first participants had 5 tasks)
  group_by(participant_code) %>%
  mutate(some_exclusion = 
         ifelse(any(ccei < 0.8, # Flag participants with at least one exclusion criterion (easier to filter for them later)
                unipref != 0, 
                minutes_on_experiment <= 5, 
                minutes_on_experiment >= 120, 
                comprehension_errors_hidden >= 10), 1, 0)) %>%
  filter(
        ccei >= 0.8,
         unipref == 0,
         minutes_on_experiment > 5,
         minutes_on_experiment < 120,
         comprehension_errors_hidden < 10
         )

partially_eligible_subjects <- eligible_tasks %>%
  distinct(participant_code, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(!c(task_number, unipref, ccei))
```

```{r exclusion-reporting}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helper for the manuscript exclusion paragraph.
#
# IMPORTANT: the criteria are applied in the SAME ORDER as the manuscript
# (age -> gender -> time -> comprehension -> GARP/CCEI -> unipref). Each
# percentage is taken over the sample that REMAINS after all earlier criteria,
# so this is a sequential cascade, not six independent shares. Participant-level
# criteria (age, gender, time, comprehension) remove a participant and all of
# their decision blocks; block-level criteria (CCEI, unipref) remove single
# participant-decision blocks (= goal-pair observations).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
report_base <- quality_controls %>%
  filter(participant_code %in% completes$participant_code) %>%
  group_by(participant_code) %>% filter(n() < 5) %>% ungroup() %>% # drop the 60 early 5-task pilots
  left_join(y = survey_data[, c("participant_code", "gender", "age")], by = "participant_code")

n_subj  <- function(d) dplyr::n_distinct(d$participant_code)
n_block <- function(d) nrow(d)

df <- report_base
report <- character(0)

# 1. Age < 18 (participant level, reported as a count)
report <- c(report, sprintf("Age < 18:             %d participants",
                            n_subj(df %>% filter(age < 18))))
df <- df %>% filter(age >= 18)

# 2. Gender other than male/female (participant level, count)
report <- c(report, sprintf("Gender != male/female: %d participants",
                            n_subj(df %>% filter(!(gender %in% c("male", "female"))))))
df <- df %>% filter(gender %in% c("male", "female"))

# 3. Time < 5 min or > 2 h (participant level, %)
den <- n_subj(df)
bad <- n_subj(df %>% filter(minutes_on_experiment <= 5 | minutes_on_experiment >= 120))
report <- c(report, sprintf("Time <=5 | >=120 min:  %d / %d participants = %.2f%%", bad, den, 100 * bad / den))
df <- df %>% filter(minutes_on_experiment > 5, minutes_on_experiment < 120)

# 4. Comprehension errors >= 10 (participant level, %)
den <- n_subj(df)
bad <- n_subj(df %>% filter(comprehension_errors_hidden >= 10))
report <- c(report, sprintf("Comprehension >= 10:   %d / %d participants = %.2f%%", bad, den, 100 * bad / den))
df <- df %>% filter(comprehension_errors_hidden < 10)

# 5. GARP violation, CCEI < 0.8 (participant-decision-block level, %)
den <- n_block(df)
bad <- n_block(df %>% filter(ccei < 0.8))
report <- c(report, sprintf("CCEI < 0.8 (GARP):     %d / %d blocks = %.2f%%", bad, den, 100 * bad / den))
df <- df %>% filter(ccei >= 0.8)

# 6. Near-corner allocations, unipref != 0 (goal-pair level, %)
den <- n_block(df)
bad <- n_block(df %>% filter(unipref != 0))
report <- c(report, sprintf("unipref != 0 (>=98%%):  %d / %d goal-pair obs = %.2f%%", bad, den, 100 * bad / den))
df <- df %>% filter(unipref == 0)

cat(paste(report, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
cat(sprintf("Remaining eligible (pre-representative-draw): %d participants, %d blocks\n",
            n_subj(df), n_block(df)))
```

# Select the sample for the analysis {.hidden .unnumbered .unlisted}
We oversampled for some countries and genders. For the main analysis we therefore draw a random sample such that we have the have the maximum number of eligible participants but still maintain a representative sample by gender in each country.

```{r}
# Calculate gender shares based on UN Population Dataset (already reduced to sample countries)
representative_shares <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "1_raw", "UN Population Data", "unpopulation_dataportal_20231016133527.csv")) %>%
    group_by(Location, Iso2, Sex) %>%
    summarize(n = sum(Value)) %>%
    filter(Sex %in% c("Female", "Male")) %>%
    group_by(Location) %>%
    mutate(target_share = n/sum(n), Sex = tolower(Sex)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    rename(gender = Sex, country_abrv = Iso2) %>%
    mutate(country_abrv = ifelse(country_abrv == "JP", "JA", country_abrv),
           country_abrv = ifelse(country_abrv == "NG", "NI", country_abrv)) %>%
    select(country_abrv, gender, target_share)

# Draw a representative (country x gender) random sample from a pool of eligible subjects.
# `subjects` is one row per eligible participant; `tasks` supplies the participant-task pairs.
# Refactored into a function so the same draw can be reused for the main sample and for the
# fully-rational sensitivity sample below.
draw_representative_sample <- function(subjects, tasks, seed = 123) {
    # Initiate the sample selection dataset
    sel <- subjects %>%
        left_join(y = completes[, c("participant_code", "session_label")], by = c("participant_code")) %>%
        left_join(y = country_abrv[, c("session_label", "country_abrv")], by = c("session_label")) %>%
        left_join(y = survey_data[, c("participant_code", "gender", "age")], by = c("participant_code")) %>%
        filter(age >= 18) %>% # Exclude participants with age < 18 (see the `exclusion-reporting` chunk for counts/percentages)
        filter(gender == "male" | gender =="female") %>% # Exclude participants with gender other than "Male" / "Female"
        select(participant_code, country_abrv, gender)

    # Calculate max number of participants to draw from each country and add to dataset
    sel <- sel %>% # Count total number of eligible participants in each country-gender group
        group_by(country_abrv, gender) %>%
        distinct(participant_code) %>%
        count(name = "completes") %>%
        left_join(y = representative_shares, by = c("country_abrv", "gender")) %>% # Add target shares
        group_by(country_abrv) %>% # Calculate the number of participants to draw from each country
        mutate(country_possible_draw = floor(min(completes/target_share)),
               to_draw = floor(country_possible_draw*target_share)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        select(country_abrv, gender, to_draw) %>% # Add to the main dataset
        right_join(y = sel, by = c("country_abrv", "gender"))

    # Draw the sample
    set.seed(seed) # Set seed for reproducibility
    sel %>%
        group_by(country_abrv, gender) %>%
        group_modify(~ slice_sample(.x, n = .x$to_draw[1])) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        select(participant_code, country_abrv, gender) %>%
        left_join(y = tasks[, c("participant_code", "task_number")], by = c("participant_code"))
}

# Main sample (unchanged): draw from all eligible subjects
main_sample_selection <- draw_representative_sample(partially_eligible_subjects, eligible_tasks)
write_csv(main_sample_selection, here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "main_sample_selection.csv"))

# Fully-rational sensitivity sample: keep only participants without a single excluded block
fully_rational_subjects <- eligible_tasks %>%
    filter(some_exclusion == 0) %>%
    distinct(participant_code, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    select(!c(task_number, unipref, ccei))
fully_rational_tasks <- eligible_tasks %>% filter(some_exclusion == 0)
main_sample_selection_fullyrational <- draw_representative_sample(fully_rational_subjects, fully_rational_tasks)
write_csv(main_sample_selection_fullyrational, here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "main_sample_selection_fullyrational.csv"))

# Unipref sensitivity sample: same drawn participants as the main sample, but additionally
# re-include their decision blocks that were excluded solely due to unipref (corner solutions).
# These blocks still pass CCEI/time/comprehension; only the unipref filter is relaxed.
eligible_tasks_incl_unipref <- quality_controls %>%
    filter(participant_code %in% completes$participant_code) %>%
    group_by(participant_code) %>% filter(n() < 5) %>% ungroup() %>%
    filter(ccei >= 0.8,
           minutes_on_experiment > 5,
           minutes_on_experiment < 120,
           comprehension_errors_hidden < 10) # unipref intentionally NOT filtered here

main_sample_selection_unipref <- main_sample_selection %>%
    distinct(participant_code, country_abrv, gender) %>%
    left_join(y = eligible_tasks_incl_unipref[, c("participant_code", "task_number")], by = c("participant_code"))
write_csv(main_sample_selection_unipref, here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "main_sample_selection_unipref.csv"))
```
